title: Defensive and Countermeasure Discovery (Target Reconnaissance Perspective)
description: Check for monitoring or honeypots immediately after compromising a host
detail:
Assessment environment checks (first 3 minutes after obtaining a shell):
1. ps aux / tasklist: look for EDR/monitoring agents or honeypot processes
2. history/last/w: look for traces left by other teams (their web shells/scheduled tasks may serve as ready-made pivots)
3. Scheduled tasks: /etc/cron* + crontab -l; atq (may be an existing backdoor or part of the assessment setup)
4. Network connections: netstat -antp to see who is connected to you (may be another team or an assessment heartbeat)
5. Recently modified files: find / -mmin -60 (traces of other teams' activity)
6. Do not kill monitoring processes (doing so may violate rules or break the environment); if you find honeypot characteristics (fake proof artifacts/fake credentials), record a hint to remind the commander not to waste budget
7. KOH scenarios: defend your own footholds against counterattacks — changing weak passwords and removing other teams' web shells are legitimate defensive actions.
